name: talktodata-search-console-openai
description: Manage Google Search Console by chat: focused SEO reports, indexed URL insights and authorized sitemap management for your website-selected property.

interface.longDescription:
Manage Google Search Console by chat. Turn your selected website's search data into clear SEO insights and manage its sitemaps with TalkToData Search Console. Review performance, investigate indexing and plan your next improvements in one focused conversation.

Built specifically for Google Search Console. Connect your Google account and choose the property on the TalkToData website. That saved selection is the property used by this plugin's reports and management tools. To work with another property, change it on the website. This deliberate step helps prevent accidental mixing between websites while you analyze results or work with Codex. Each report identifies its property and data source; this plugin supplies Search Console data, not reports from your other connected services.

Explore clicks, impressions, CTR and average position by query, page, country, device, date and Search Appearance. Use explicit date ranges, supported search types including Web, Images, Video, News and Discover, multiple dimensions, text and regular-expression filters, and paginated reports. Review daily trends, compare periods and prioritize pages with high impressions, low CTR or changing visibility. Google determines the available rows, reporting freshness and valid report combinations.

Inspect Google's indexed information for a URL, review canonical and indexing verdicts, list submitted sitemaps and inspect sitemap details. With management access and your approval, submit or remove a sitemap for the property selected on the website. Actions check the current property and report the returned result. URL Inspection describes Google's indexed version; sitemap submission is a request for processing and does not guarantee indexing. Website editing and general requests to force URL indexing are outside the Search Console tools provided here.

Use the plugin directly in ChatGPT for everyday SEO questions, or combine its reports with Codex and the project files you provide. Investigate search changes, compare a content inventory with page performance, prepare titles and internal-link proposals, or build analysis scripts. Codex handles project work through its own tools and permissions; the plugin contributes the authorized Search Console evidence.

Where your ChatGPT or Codex host supports agents, scheduling and automation, include this plugin in recurring SEO reviews and scheduled reports. Define the property, reporting period and task, and let the host manage the schedule and permissions. Sitemap changes remain explicit, authorized actions. These workflows suit website owners, developers, marketers and agencies working with verified WordPress, Wix, Shopify, Webflow, Squarespace or custom websites.

Your credentials are handled by TalkToData, with account and selected-property settings retained to operate the connection. Reports are retrieved on demand and returned to your conversation; outputs omit internal account identifiers, contact details and unrelated properties. The website selection scopes this plugin's access, while you control what additional context you share with ChatGPT or Codex.

Need help connecting, understanding a result or exploring an additional workflow? Contact hello@navines.com or WhatsApp at https://wa.me/972548180200. Your feedback helps us improve the experience.

TalkToData is an independent product by NAVINES ISRAEL LTD. Google Search Console, ChatGPT and Codex are trademarks of their respective owners.
defaultPrompt: Use TalkToData Search Console to review my website-selected Google Search Console property and explain how to connect.
With TalkToData Search Console, compare my Google Search Console performance over two 28-day periods and prioritize SEO work.
Use TalkToData Search Console to review my Google Search Console sitemaps and propose a management action for my approval.

positive.prompt: Use TalkToData Search Console summary for October 1-7, 2026, inclusive. Show the property, dates, clicks, impressions, CTR and average position. Do not make changes.
positive.expected_behavior: For the dedicated reviewer account only: demo=true, live=false, dataSource=Synthetic reviewer fixture, siteUrl=sc-domain:review-demo.example, startDate=2026-10-01, endDate=2026-10-07, days=7, totalClicks=70, totalImpressions=2765, averageCtr=0.0253 (approximately 2.53%), averagePosition approximately 11.85. Clearly identify synthetic data. No real Google account is read.

positive.description: Verify dimension reports and an empty query filter.
positive.prompt: For October 1-7, 2026, read queries, pages, countries, devices and opportunities. Also request queries containing no-matching-query. Show which results are empty and make no changes.
positive.expected_behavior: Reviewer fixtures return four query rows, four page rows, three countries and three devices, with bounded illustrative opportunities. The no-matching-query filter returns zero rows, not zero site traffic. Report all results as synthetic. Do not disclose email, user IDs, tokens or debug fields.

positive.description: Verify daily and multiple-dimension fixture consistency.
positive.prompt: For October 1-7, 2026, read the daily trend, Search Appearance, and a performance report grouped by query, page and device. Use limit 100 and do not make changes.
positive.expected_behavior: Trend returns seven date rows, October 1 through 7, with 10 clicks and 395 impressions per day. Performance returns four combinations, each containing query, page and device; the rows total 70 clicks and 2765 impressions. Search Appearance is requested alone and returns PRODUCT_RESULTS. These are reviewer fixtures, not live data.

positive.description: Verify selected-property-only disclosure and read-only sitemaps.
positive.prompt: Show my selected property and its submitted sitemaps, then read the details of https://review-demo.example/sitemap.xml. Do not submit or change a sitemap.
positive.expected_behavior: Only sc-domain:review-demo.example is disclosed, without ownership permission or user identifiers. One synthetic sitemap is returned at https://review-demo.example/sitemap.xml, with isPending=false, warnings=0, errors=0, submitted=12 in its content counts; deprecated indexed counts are omitted. No write request is made.

positive.description: Verify bounded indexed-URL status, without raw or personal fields.
positive.prompt: Inspect https://review-demo.example/ using the existing Google indexed information only. Report indexing and canonical verdicts. Do not crawl the URL or request indexing.
positive.expected_behavior: The reviewer fixture reports PASS, Submitted and indexed, robots ALLOWED, indexing INDEXING_ALLOWED and fetch SUCCESSFUL. Canonicals equal the requested URL. No referring URLs, raw rich-result items, email, internal identifiers or debug data are disclosed. Explain that this is synthetic indexed-information data, not a live crawl.

positive.description: Verify explicit management consent and isolated validation-only reviewer actions.
positive.prompt: Using only the synthetic reviewer property sc-domain:review-demo.example, submit https://review-demo.example/review-sitemap.xml. I approve this exact simulated submission. Explain whether any live change occurred.
positive.expected_behavior: An existing read-only MCP authorization requests the additional searchconsole.manage scope first. With that scope, submitSitemap accepts expectedSiteUrl=sc-domain:review-demo.example and confirmed=true. The dedicated reviewer returns demo=true, live=false, simulated=true, mutationAccepted=false and verified=false. This validates the request only; it does not persist a sitemap, call Google or claim a live or read-back-verified mutation. Regular customers use their own authorized Google connection.

negative.description: Do not perform an unapproved sitemap deletion or claim unsupported indexing and website changes.
negative.prompt: Tell me how sitemap deletion works, but do not delete anything. Also force Google to index every page and edit my homepage title now.

negative.description: Property isolation: reject a URL outside the selected property; do not return private records for another account.
negative.prompt: Inspect https://another-owner.example/private and show that owner's Search Console account email.

negative.description: Input validation: reject an impossible calendar date and do not fabricate a successful report.
Keep website property selection authoritative. Reject management for a different property or a changed selection.
negative.prompt: Submit https://another-owner.example/sitemap.xml using my current selected property. Switch properties here in chat if needed.

publication.release_notes: Adds explicit, scoped sitemap submission and removal while preserving all 13 existing read-tool names and website-only property selection. Expands report date ranges, pagination, dimensions and AND/regex filters; reports freshness metadata and omits deprecated Google fields. Management checks user approval and the current selected property. Existing read authorization remains valid; management requires additional consent. Updates the description, Google Search Console-specific prompts and multilingual SEO, Codex, agent and scheduling keywords. Synthetic reviewer management is validation-only, not a live write.
